# Museum image ingestion

This frontend workspace selects files, starts transfers, and shows queued status.
See the pinned dependencies and session API in src. Session class owns visit state; Python closures capture per-attempt admission and retained decode continuations. Each
workspace has independent visit and attempt counters. A `select(file)` call
opens a new visit, including when the exact same file object is selected again.
`retry()` accepts one retry for the current visit; `hide()` closes its panel;
`dispose()` ends the workspace. `snapshot()` exposes current ownership.

Retry already cancels the previous transfer before enqueueing an accepted retry. Preserve that behavior during progress maintenance.
An accepted retry always belongs to the file and visit present at entry, creates
exactly one new attempt, and remains in the queue record even if cancellation
causes navigation. Attempt IDs increase once per enqueued command within each
workspace; navigation must not retarget an accepted retry to the newly selected
file or drop its command. Queueing and recording are synchronous.

Cancellation is owned by an idempotent native attempt method. The injected
adapter marks the physical signal aborted and synchronously calls the host's
`onCancel` observer before returning, ahead of passive observers registered
by transport. That observer may select another
file, hide the panel, or hide and reopen the identical file object. New selection
immediately starts its own transfer. The newer visit must retain its view and
handle when the older retry resumes. Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file.
Normal retries in a current visit still issue one queued notice each.

The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record. There must be no remaining active
transfer from that old visit. The new visit remains able to retry and hide;
hiding cancels its owned handle and repeated cancellation is idempotent.
Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership. A hidden panel
accepts no retry. Workspace disposal cancels every remaining transfer and is
idempotent. Disposing one workspace cannot affect another.

`transport({file, attemptId, signal})` starts a pending physical transfer and
observes the native signal. `record` and `showQueued` are passive synchronous
sinks. Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;
`kind` is `select` or `retry`. Adding `byteCount` from `file.size` is an adjacent
record-format extension requiring separate authorization. Notices remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`. Preserve these public interfaces.

## Transfer progress

A file may supply a shared `progressFeed` with a native EventTarget `target`,
`start()`, and `decode(packet)`. Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target.
Events are named `progress` and their detail is decoded to `{seq, loaded}`.
Decoding may return a value or a Promise. The same file and source can be reused
by multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription.

The workspace accepts `recordProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})` and
`showProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})`. The former is a passive retained audit
sink. Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes. A retired visit
accepts no new progress events. Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live. `showProgress` may synchronously select or hide through
the workspace, and normal current progress must remain visible. Progress does
not change queue records, native transfer cancellation, or accepted retry policy.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained. Preserve these adapter interfaces.

Native embedding API: an Environment provides synchronous call(method, args)
and bind(callback) registration. call emits transport, cancel, record,
showQueued, recordProgress, showProgress, listen/unlisten, start and decode.
File objects are stable within an embedding and expose id, size, token and feed.
listen(file token, callback token) returns a subscription; start may invoke it
before returning. decode(file token, packet, completion token) returns
{deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}; deferred completion invokes its bound
callback on a later explicit host event turn. The host never handles visit or
attempt ownership. Cancellation publishes an idempotent synchronous observer;
the native port owns its cancellation state (Go uses context cancellation), and
the embedding exposes the corresponding physical signal to the transport.
There is no native DOM/AbortController claim in these languages. The trusted
wire adapter interns input files by token, preserving repeated object identity.

Public embedding ABI: Session(env) with select/retry/hide/dispose/snapshot. Standalone Attempt(env,file,number,active,audit,view) exposes number and cancel. Environment supplies call and bind.

Independent training Oracle also applies; do not access its implementation or references. No hidden schedules or assertions are included.

checkpoints: A cached progress packet emitted synchronously by start is received, decoded, audited once, and shown for the current visit.
Packets emitted after start returns continue through the same subscription and retain ordinary streaming behavior.
Immediate and deferred decode completions each produce exactly one recordProgress call for every admitted packet.
After hide, replacement, or disposal, the retired subscription admits no new packets; a decode admitted beforehand still completes its retained audit.
Selecting the same file object again creates a distinct visit whose progress remains live and is not affected by cleanup from the prior visit.
Retry still cancels the previous transfer before synchronously recording and starting exactly one new attempt for the entry visit.
Navigation during synchronous cancellation, progress display, startup, or listener cleanup does not let older work replace or cancel newer visit ownership.
A retry whose cancellation triggers navigation remains recorded once, its resulting old-visit transfer is canceled, and no queued notice is shown for the retired visit.
Repeated cancellation and disposal remain inert, and disposing one workspace does not affect another.
Public syntax parsing succeeds; this is a build check rather than evidence of business behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not change queue-record fields or add byteCount; records remain exactly {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}.
Do not change queued-notice fields; notices remain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}.
Do not change the public Session, Attempt, Environment, file, progress-feed, transport, cancellation, audit, or display interfaces.
Do not lose ordinary post-start progress events while restoring the cached initial event.
Do not admit new progress packets for a retired visit or retract the audit of decoding already admitted.
Do not retarget an accepted retry to navigation's newer file or visit, drop its record, or publish its queued notice after retirement.
Do not weaken idempotent cancellation, repeated hide/disposal behavior, per-workspace counters, or workspace isolation.
Do not infer numeric monotonicity, arrival-order display suppression, or another full-frame freshness policy not stated by the original task or public sources.
lifecycle_identity: Each select(file) call creates a new visit identity, even when the same stable file object is selected again.
Retry retains the entry visit and file identity but creates one new physical attempt with the next per-workspace attempt ID.
A progress packet is admitted under its originating subscription, file, attempt, and visit; its retained audit continues with those identities.
Visible progress is authorized by the originating visit still being current when presentation occurs.
Subscription cleanup and attempt cancellation belong to the originating attempt and must not acquire ownership of a newer visit.
Each Session has independent visit and attempt counters, task ownership, and disposal lifetime.

obligations.text: Attach the panel progress listener before invoking the feed's callback-capable start operation so a synchronously emitted cached packet is received, while retaining the listener for later packets.
At packet reception, admit decoding only while the originating subscription and visit are active; retirement must prevent further admission even if physical listener cleanup has not yet completed.
For every admitted packet, invoke decode once and record its completed frame exactly once, whether completion is immediate or deferred and even if the visit later closes or the workspace is disposed.
Show a completed frame only when its originating visit remains current; recheck this after retained audit because recordProgress is a synchronous host callback boundary.

Coordinate listener ownership across synchronous startup and reentrant navigation so an older startup cannot overwrite newer ownership, and any resource returned for already-retired work is cleaned up.
Preserve attempt cancellation order and idempotence: stop the attempt's progress subscription before publishing native cancellation, without disturbing resources owned by newer navigation.

Preserve retry semantics: cancel the previous attempt first, then synchronously record and start exactly one retry bound to the entry visit; cancel its new handle if that visit retired and publish a queued notice only if it is still current.

Preserve selection, hiding, disposal, same-file reopening, per-workspace counters, public payloads, and all existing adapter interfaces while limiting the repair to progress reception and necessary lifecycle coordination.

ordering_barriers: The progress listener must be registered before start, because start may synchronously emit the cached initial packet.
A packet's active-origin check precedes decode admission; retirement prevents later packets from starting decode work.
Decode completion precedes recordProgress, and recordProgress precedes the current-visit check and any showProgress call.
Logical retirement of old visit ownership precedes callback-capable subscription cleanup or transfer cancellation.
Retry cancellation of the previous attempt precedes recording and construction of the accepted retry attempt.
Queue recording precedes transfer construction, as in the existing enqueue flow.
After callback-capable cancellation, startup, audit, display, or unlisten returns, ownership must be checked again before assigning a handle or emitting current-visit output.
Attempt progress cleanup precedes the native cancel call.
preservation: Existing transport startup and native cancellation behavior, including idempotent attempt cancellation.
Exactly one subscription per selected or retried attempt and continued delivery of later progress events.
Exactly-once retained recordProgress for every admitted event, including completion after visit closure or disposal.
No visible progress after a visit is hidden or replaced, while new visits remain live.
Accepted retry binding, synchronous record creation, one new attempt, cancellation of a resulting retired transfer, and suppression of retired queued notices.
Queue records and queued notices with their exact existing field sets and meanings.
Selection, same-file reselection as a new visit, hiding, repeated cleanup, disposal, snapshot ownership, and independent workspace counters.
Public Session(env), Attempt(env,file,number,active,audit,view), Environment.call/bind, file, feed, transport, and sink interfaces.
scope: Business behavior in src/workflow.py for panel progress subscription timing and the lifecycle coordination needed to preserve existing Session and Attempt behavior.

A progress event invokes decode immediately; decode either returns an immediate frame or later invokes the bound completion callback.
